answer: We formalize a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices impose a rising entry threshold for node propagation. Integrating zero-knowledge verifiable delay with staking collateral proves that slashing penalties create a mirror of an adversary's commitment, rendering expected Sybil multiplication utility strictly negative. This Nash equilibrium stabilizes as ivory barriers to distinct identities exceed any plume of protocol rewards, securing environments against rational multi-agent collusion.
